failed.question:
An art thief planned to steal a three-dimensional piece of hanging installation art from a modern art museum. Her plan involved dressing up like a museum docent, temporarily closing off the room that contained the installation art, and in the one minute it took for the security camera to visually sweep the rest of the room, hiding the installation art in a covered garbage can. Before the police or museum security would think to search a garbage can, the art thief would then disguise herself as part of the janitorial crew and remove the garbage can containing the installation art from the museum. However, on the day she planned to execute her heist, the art thief found out that the museum had recently installed hidden GPS tracking devices on all of the art pieces in the museum. The art thief decided to postpone her heist until she could figure out how to disable the GPS device and avoid getting caught. A few days later, the art thief was arrested by the police based on security footage from the museum that showed the art thief engaged in suspicious activities like stealing docent and janitorial uniforms and timing the security cameras.
Can the art thief be charged with attempted larceny of the artwork?

A man told his girlfriend that he was planning to rob a 24-hour convenience store and would split the proceeds from the robbery if she agreed to drive the getaway car. The girlfriend agreed and drove the man to the store so he could commit the robbery. While the man was holding up the cashier in the store, the man's gun went off accidentally, killing the cashier. The man left through the exit at the back of the store without taking any money, leaving the girlfriend in the car outside the store to be arrested when the police arrived.
For which of the following crimes may the girlfriend properly be convicted and punished?

An 18-year-old female and a 15-year-old male, who had known each other since early childhood, agreed to have sexual intercourse and did so. The applicable jurisdiction defines rape as "sexual intercourse with another person (i) without that person's consent or (ii) who is less than 16 years old." This jurisdiction also follows the common-law approach to conspiracy.
Can the female properly be charged with conspiracy to commit rape?

A jurisdiction has the following decisional law on questions of principal and accomplice liability:
CASE A: The defendant, a hardware store owner, sold several customers a device which detects police radar and enables speeders to avoid detection. When one of the devices broke down and the speeder was arrested, he confessed that he often sped, secure in the knowledge that the device would warn him of police radar in the vicinity. Held: The defendant is guilty as an accomplice to speeding.
CASE B: The defendant told a friend that the defendant had stored some stereo equipment in a self-storage locker. He gave the friend a key and asked her to pick up the equipment and deliver it to the defendant's house. The friend complied and removed the equipment from the locker using the key. In fact, the equipment belonged to the defendant's neighbor, whose locker key the defendant had found in the driveway. Held: The defendant is guilty as a principal to burglary.
CASE C: A city council member accepted a bribe from the defendant in exchange for his vote on the defendant's application for a zoning variance. A statute prohibits the taking of bribes by public officials. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to the city council member's violation of the bribery statute.
CASE D: The defendant, an innkeeper, sometimes let his rooms to prostitutes whom he knew to be using the rooms to ply their trade. He charged the prostitutes the same price as other guests at his inn. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to prostitution.
A plastic surgeon agreed to remove the fingerprints from the hands of a man whom the surgeon knew to be a safecracker. The surgeon charged his usual hourly rate for the operation. Afterward, the man burglarized a bank safe and was convicted of burglary. The surgeon has been charged with burglary.
Should he be convicted or acquitted of this crime?

A jurisdiction has the following decisional law on questions of principal and accomplice liability:
CASE A: The defendant, a hardware store owner, sold several customers a device which detects police radar and enables speeders to avoid detection. When one of the devices broke down and the speeder was arrested, he confessed that he often sped, secure in the knowledge that the device would warn him of police radar in the vicinity. Held: The defendant is guilty as an accomplice to speeding.
CASE B: The defendant told a friend that the defendant had stored some stereo equipment in a self-storage locker. He gave the friend a key and asked her to pick up the equipment and deliver it to the defendant's house. The friend complied and removed the equipment from the locker using the key. In fact, the equipment belonged to the defendant's neighbor, whose locker key the defendant had found in the driveway. Held: The defendant is guilty as a principal to burglary.
CASE C: A city council member accepted a bribe from the defendant in exchange for his vote on the defendant's application for a zoning variance. A statute prohibits the taking of bribes by public officials. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to the city council member's violation of the bribery statute.
CASE D: The defendant, an innkeeper, sometimes lent his rooms to prostitutes whom he knew to be using the rooms to ply their trade. He charged the prostitutes the same price as other guests at his inn. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to prostitution.
In this jurisdiction, conviction for statutory rape requires proof of the defendant's knowledge that the victim is underage. A high school student, who knew that a girl was underage, encouraged his friend, who was unaware of the girl's age, to have sex with the girl. The student has been charged with statutory rape.
Should the student be convicted or acquitted of this crime?

A man and a woman agreed to engage in sexual intercourse at a particular hotel the following night. The man, who was the son of the woman's brother-in-law, rented the hotel room for their tryst, but the woman did not show up.
In the applicable jurisdiction, a statute provides that a person commits the offense of incest when such person engages in sexual intercourse with a person whom he or she knows he or she is related to either by blood or by marriage as aunt or nephew.
Can the woman and the man properly be charged with conspiracy to commit incest?

A retailer sponsored a game that required individuals to collect game pieces in order to win various monetary prizes. An employee of the retailer embezzled the rare game pieces necessary for the significant monetary prizes. The employee then separately contacted various individuals, each of whom was given a rare game piece. The employee did not disclose, and the individuals did not learn, that the employee gave game pieces to anyone else. Each individual then submitted the necessary game pieces, including the rare game piece provided by the employee, to the retailer for a monetary prize. In order to obtain a prize, each individual falsely stated that he had obtained all of the game pieces through authorized, legitimate channels. Upon receipt of the prize money, each individual paid 50 percent of the money to the employee, as previously agreed.
Among other offenses, the employee and all of the individuals were charged with entering into a single conspiracy to obtain money from the retailer by false pretenses.
Can the defendants properly be convicted of this conspiracy?

A construction company sent a bill to a customer who had hired the company to do work on the customer's home. The bill contained charges for material and labor for construction that was done on the personal residence of the company's president, rather than the customer's home. The customer paid the bill, believing it was for his home. Subsequently, the company and its president were charged with the crime of conspiring to commit theft as well as the crime of theft. The customer lived in the state that was prosecuting these crimes. The company was incorporated in another state and its president lived in that state. Each defendant was convicted of both crimes.
The theft crime is statutorily defined as follows: "A person commits the offense of theft if the person obtains property of another by deception." The conspiracy crime is statutorily defined as follows: "A person commits the offense of conspiracy to commit theft when the person agrees with another to commit theft of any property that belongs to another." Both crimes include a legal entity within the definition of "person."
The company and its president have appealed their convictions for the conspiracy offense only. Which of the following is their best defense to this crime?

A hair technician agreed to implant synthetic hair into the scalp of her customer. The customer explained to the hair technician that he often broke into people's houses to take jewelry and that he wanted to avoid leaving his own hair at the scene as incriminating evidence. The technician, knowing that a great deal of the synthetic hair would fall out due to implant rejection, that the strands would still have the customer's DNA at the root, and that the procedure would be no help at all in hiding forensic evidence, said nothing. The technician completed the procedure and charged her regular hourly rate. The next night, the customer broke into a house and stole a diamond ring. He later was convicted of burglary based on hair evidence he left behind.
The jurisdiction follows the Model Penal Code rule regarding accomplice liability.
Should the hair technician be convicted of burglary as an accomplice?

questions.question:
A woman wanted to kill a business competitor. She contacted a man who she believed was willing to commit murder for hire and offered him $50,000 to kill the competitor. The man agreed to do so and accepted $25,000 as a down payment. Unbeknownst to the woman, the man was an undercover police officer.
In a jurisdiction that has adopted the unilateral theory of conspiracy, is the woman guilty of conspiracy to murder the business competitor?

choices.a: No, because it would have been impossible for the woman to kill the competitor by this method.
choices.b: No, because the man did not intend to kill the competitor.
choices.c: Yes, because the woman believed that she had an agreement with the man that would bring about the competitor's death.
choices.d: Yes, because the woman took a substantial step toward bringing about the competitor's death by paying the man $25,000.

data.questionStem:
Q84084

A woman wanted to kill a business competitor. She contacted a man who she believed was willing to commit murder for hire and offered him $50,000 to kill the competitor. The man agreed to do so and accepted $25,000 as a down payment. Unbeknownst to the woman, the man was an undercover police officer.

In a jurisdiction that has adopted the unilateral theory of conspiracy, is the woman guilty of conspiracy to murder the business competitor?

一名女子想杀死一名商业竞争对手。她联系了一名她认为愿意受雇杀人的男子，并向他要约支付50,000美元以杀死该竞争对手。该男子同意了，并接受了25,000美元作为定金。该女子不知道的是，这名男子是一名卧底警察。

在一个采纳了共谋单方理论的司法管辖区内，该女子是否犯有共谋谋杀该商业竞争对手的罪行？
options:
A. No, because it would have been impossible for the woman to kill the competitor by this method.
不成立，因为该女子通过这种方法杀死竞争对手是不可能的。

B. No, because the man did not intend to kill the competitor.
不成立，因为该男子并无意图杀死该竞争对手。

C. Yes, because the woman believed that she had an agreement with the man that would bring about the competitor's death.
成立，因为该女子相信她与该男子达成了一项会导致竞争对手死亡的协议。

D. Yes, because the woman took a substantial step toward bringing about the competitor's death by paying the man $25,000.
成立，因为该女子通过支付该男子25,000美元，为导致竞争对手的死亡采取了实质性步骤。
data.explanation:
Conspiracy


AgreementOvert act
Majority view (modern & MPC)Unilateral approach - at least one person specifically intends to enter agreementAt least one conspirator must commit overt act
Minority view (common law)Bilateral approach - two or more persons specifically intend to enter agreementNot required
MPC = Model Penal Code.

Conspiracy occurs when:
  • two or more persons enter an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime and
  • in most jurisdictions, an overt act is committed in furtherance of that agreement.

The common law bilateral theory of conspiracy required proof of at least two guilty minds, so a defendant could not be convicted if the other conspirators had feigned agreement. But most jurisdictions now follow the unilateral theory of conspiracy, where only one guilty mind is required. That means a defendant can be convicted even if the other conspirators feigned agreement to commit the crime.

Here, the woman hired a man to kill her business competitor (agreement and intent) and gave him a $25,000 down payment (overt act). Therefore, the woman is guilty under the unilateral theory of conspiracy even though the man (an undercover police officer) did not intend to commit the crime. But had this jurisdiction followed the bilateral theory of conspiracy, the man's feigned agreement would have absolved the woman of this crime (Choice B).

(Choice A) It would have been impossible for the woman to kill the competitor by this method since the man was an undercover police officer. But the woman is still guilty since factual impossibility is no defense to conspiracy.

(Choice D) Most jurisdictions require proof of an overt act to convict a defendant of attempt or conspiracy. While attempt requires proof of a substantial step - ie, conduct strongly corroborating criminal intent (more than mere preparation) - conspiracy only requires discernible evidence that the conspiracy is at work (including acts of mere preparation). Here, the woman's $25,000 down payment is an overt act under both standards. But it would only support her conviction if an overt act is an element of conspiracy in this jurisdiction.

Educational objective: The unilateral theory of conspiracy requires only one guilty mind, so a defendant is guilty even if the other conspirators feigned agreement to commit the crime. But since the bilateral theory requires two guilty minds, a defendant would not be guilty if the other conspirators feigned agreement.

选项正确率统计：A选项 0%，B选项 2%，C选项 69%（正确选项），D选项 27%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

共谋


协议公开行为
多数观点 (现代 & MPC)单方理论 - 至少一人有特定意图订立协议至少一名共谋者必须实施公开行为
少数观点 (普通法)双方理论 - 两人或以上有特定意图订立协议不要求
MPC = Model Penal Code.

共谋罪在以下情况成立：
  • 两人或以上怀有实施犯罪的特定意图而达成协议，并且
  • 在大多数司法管辖区，为推进该协议而实施了公开行为。

普通法中的共谋双方理论要求证明至少存在两个有罪意图，因此如果其他共谋者只是假装同意，被告则不能被定罪。但现在大多数司法管辖区遵循共谋的单方理论，该理论只要求一个有罪意图。这意味着即使其他共谋者假装同意实施犯罪，被告也可以被定罪。

在本案中，该女子雇佣一名男子杀死她的商业竞争对手（协议和意图），并向他支付了25,000美元的定金（公开行为）。因此，根据共谋的单方理论，尽管该男子（一名卧底警察）并无意图实施犯罪，该女子仍构成共谋罪。但是，如果该司法管辖区遵循共谋的双方理论，那么该男子的假装同意将使该女子免于此罪责 (选项 B)。

(选项 A) 由于该男子是一名卧底警察，该女子通过这种方法杀死竞争对手是不可能的。但该女子仍然有罪，因为事实不能不是共谋罪的有效抗辩理由。

(选项 D) 大多数司法管辖区要求证明存在公开行为才能将被告定为未遂罪或共谋罪。未遂罪要求证明存在实质性步骤——即，能有力证实犯罪意图的行为（而不仅是预备行为）——而共谋罪仅要求有可识别的证据表明共谋正在进行中（包括仅为预备的行为）。在本案中，该女子支付的25,000美元定金，根据这两种标准都构成公开行为。但只有在该司法管辖区将公开行为作为共谋罪的一个构成要件时，这才能支持对她的定罪。

教学目标：共谋的单方理论只要求一个有罪意图，因此即使其他共谋者假装同意实施犯罪，被告也构成犯罪。但由于双方理论要求两个有罪意图，如果其他共谋者假装同意，被告则不构成犯罪。

References

  • 16 Am. Jur. 2d Conspiracy § 16 (2019) (unilateral theory of conspiracy).
  • Model Penal Code § 5.03 (Am. Law Inst. 2019) (criminal conspiracy).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点精讲

Criminal Law: Conspiracy
核心考点：共谋的单方理论 (Unilateral Theory) 本题考察的是共谋罪（Conspiracy）中关于“协议”（Agreement）认定的两种不同理论。这是MBE刑法部分的高频考点。
普通法 (Common Law) - 双方理论 (Bilateral Theory)
要求至少两人拥有真实的犯罪意图（Two Guilty Minds）。如果一方是卧底警察或假装同意，则不构成共谋。
现代法/MPC - 单方理论 (Unilateral Theory)
本题适用规则
仅要求被告人有真实的犯罪意图并相信达成了协议。即使另一方是假装的（如卧底），被告人依然构成共谋罪。
案情分析

在本案中，女子（被告）具有杀死竞争对手的特定意图（Specific Intent），并且她相信自己已经与该男子达成了协议。

尽管该男子是卧底警察（Undercover Officer），并没有真实的犯罪意图，但题目明确指出该司法管辖区采用单方理论 (Unilateral Theory)。

因此，只要被告单方面具备“意图”和“达成协议的认知”，共谋罪即成立。

选项深度解析
选项 C (正确答案)
"成立，因为该女子相信她与该男子达成了一项会导致竞争对手死亡的协议。"
这准确描述了单方理论的核心：关注被告人的主观罪过（Culpability）。只要她相信协议存在，另一方是否真心同意在所不问。
选项 B (错误 - 常见陷阱)
"不成立，因为该男子并无意图..."
这是双方理论 (Bilateral Theory) 下的抗辩理由。如果题目说这是普通法（Common Law）管辖区，这个选项才是对的。但在单方理论下，卧底警察没有意图并不影响被告的定罪。
选项 A (错误)
"事实不能 (Factual Impossibility)"
虽然因为警察卧底导致谋杀不可能成功，但在共谋罪（以及未遂罪）中，事实不能从来不是有效的抗辩理由 (No defense)。
选项 D (错误 - 混淆概念)
"实质性步骤 (Substantial Step)"
这是未遂罪 (Attempt) 的标准。共谋罪通常只需要一个公开行为 (Overt Act)，而不需要达到“实质性步骤”的程度。虽然支付定金确实是公开行为，但选项D的表述侧重于未遂罪的标准，且没有点出本题的核心考点（单方 vs 双方协议）。
💡 MBE 答题技巧
看到“卧底警察 (Undercover Police)”参与共谋，立即检查题目适用的规则：
如果是 Common Law → 无罪 (需两人)；
如果是 MPC / Unilateral → 有罪 (仅需一人)。

questions.question:
A foreign diplomat discovered that a small person could enter a particular jewelry store by crawling through an air vent. The diplomat befriended a woman he met in a bar who he believed was small enough to crawl through the air vent. Without telling her that he was a diplomat, he explained how she could get into the jewelry store. She agreed to help him burglarize the store. Someone overheard their conversation and reported it to the police. Shortly thereafter, the police arrested the diplomat and the woman. Both were charged with conspiracy to commit burglary.
Before trial, the diplomat moved to dismiss the charge against him on the ground that he was entitled to diplomatic immunity. The court granted his motion. The woman then moved to dismiss the conspiracy charge against her. The jurisdiction has adopted the Model Penal Code version of conspiracy.
Should the court grant the woman's motion to dismiss the conspiracy charge against her?

choices.a: No, because the diplomat's defense does not negate any element of the crime.
choices.b: No, because the woman was not aware of the diplomat's status.
choices.c: Yes, because a conspiracy requires two guilty participants.
choices.d: Yes, because but for the diplomat's conduct, no conspiracy would have occurred.

Q84069

A foreign diplomat discovered that a small person could enter a particular jewelry store by crawling through an air vent. The diplomat befriended a woman he met in a bar who he believed was small enough to crawl through the air vent. Without telling her that he was a diplomat, he explained how she could get into the jewelry store. She agreed to help him burglarize the store. Someone overheard their conversation and reported it to the police. Shortly thereafter, the police arrested the diplomat and the woman. Both were charged with conspiracy to commit burglary.

Before trial, the diplomat moved to dismiss the charge against him on the ground that he was entitled to diplomatic immunity. The court granted his motion. The woman then moved to dismiss the conspiracy charge against her. The jurisdiction has adopted the Model Penal Code version of conspiracy.

Should the court grant the woman's motion to dismiss the conspiracy charge against her?

一名外国外交官发现，一个身材矮小的人可以通过爬过通风口进入一家特定的珠宝店。该外交官在酒吧结识了一名女子，他认为这名女子身材足够矮小，可以爬过通风口。他没有告诉她自己是外交官，而是向她解释了如何进入珠宝店。她同意帮助他犯下入室犯法罪。有人无意中听到了他们的谈话并报了警。不久之后，警方逮捕了该外交官和该女子。两人均被指控共谋实施入室犯法罪。

在审判前，该外交官以其享有外交豁免权为由，请求驳回对他的指控。法院批准了他的请求。随后，该女子也请求驳回对她的共谋指控。该司法管辖区采纳了《Model Penal Code》中关于共谋罪的规定。

法院是否应批准该女子驳回共谋指控的请求？
options:
A. No, because the diplomat's defense does not negate any element of the crime.
不应批准，因为外交官的抗辩理由并未否定该罪行的任何构成要件。

B. No, because the woman was not aware of the diplomat's status.
不应批准，因为该女子并不知道外交官的身份。

C. Yes, because a conspiracy requires two guilty participants.
应批准，因为共谋罪要求有两名有罪的参与者。

D. Yes, because but for the diplomat's conduct, no conspiracy would have occurred.
应批准，因为若非外交官的行为，共谋便不会发生。
data.explanation:
Conspiracy


AgreementOvert act
Majority view (modern & MPC)Unilateral approach - at least one person specifically intends to enter agreementAt least one conspirator must commit overt act
Minority view (common law)Bilateral approach - two or more persons specifically intend to enter agreementNot required
MPC = Model Penal Code.

Under the Model Penal Code (MPC) and in most jurisdictions, conspiracy requires proof that:
  • a person entered into an agreement to commit a crime with the specific intent to commit that crime and
  • one of the conspirators committed an overt act in furtherance of that agreement.
This definition of conspiracy departs from the traditional view that there must be at least two guilty parties to form a conspiracy. As a result, another conspirator's guilt (or lack thereof) has no effect on the defendant's liability.

Here, the diplomat and the woman were charged with conspiracy after they agreed to burglarize a jewelry store. The conspiracy charge against the diplomat was dismissed due to his diplomatic immunity. But the diplomat's immunity defense does not affect the woman's liability for conspiracy since this MPC jurisdiction only requires proof of one guilty participant (Choice C). As a result, her motion to dismiss this charge should be denied.

It is also worth noting the 'overt act' requirement. While the facts state they had a conversation and agreed, they do not explicitly mention a subsequent overt act taken in furtherance of the conspiracy before their arrest. However, this is not a fatal flaw for two reasons. First, the MPC dispenses with the overt act requirement for conspiracies to commit the most serious felonies (typically first or second degree). The burglary of a jewelry store would almost certainly qualify as such a felony, meaning the agreement alone would be sufficient to complete the crime of conspiracy. Second, and more importantly for this question, the woman's motion to dismiss is based on the diplomat's immunity, not on the lack of an overt act. The question asks us to evaluate the validity of her specific legal argument. The core legal principle being tested here is the MPC's unilateral approach, which is why Choice A is correct. The diplomat's personal defense (immunity) does not negate any element of the crime for the woman.

(Choice B) The woman's awareness of the diplomat's status has no bearing on her liability for conspiracy.

(Choice D) Although the diplomat's conduct was a but-for cause of the conspiracy, his actions do not excuse the woman's criminal liability. Instead, those actions support her conviction since they satisfy the overt act requirement.

Educational objective: Under the Model Penal Code (MPC), conspiracy occurs when (1) a person enters into an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime and (2) any conspirator commits an overt act in furtherance of that agreement. Therefore, the MPC only requires proof of one guilty participant.

选项正确率统计：A选项 77%（正确选项），B选项 5%，C选项 14%，D选项 3%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

共谋罪


合意公开行为
多数派观点 (现代 & MPC)单边理论 - 至少有一人明确意图达成合意至少有一名共谋者必须实施公开行为
少数派观点 (普通法)双边理论 - 两人或以上明确意图达成合意不要求
MPC = 《Model Penal Code》（模范刑法典）。

根据《Model Penal Code》 (MPC) 以及大多数司法管辖区的规定，共谋罪要求证明：
  • 一人怀有实施该罪行的特定意图，与他人达成了实施犯罪的合意，并且
  • 其中一名共谋者为推进该合意而实施了公开行为。
这一定义背离了共谋罪必须至少有两名有罪方才能成立的传统观点。因此，另一名共谋者是否有罪（或无罪），不影响被告的刑事责任。

在本案中，该外交官和女子在同意实施入室犯法罪后被指控共谋。由于外交豁免权，针对外交官的共谋指控被驳回。但是，外交官的豁免权抗辩不影响该女子的共谋罪责任，因为这个采纳MPC的司法管辖区仅要求证明有一名有罪的参与者（选项C）。因此，她请求驳回此项指控的动议应被拒绝。

此外，关于“公开行为”（overt act）的要求也值得注意。虽然案情陈述了他们进行了交谈并达成了合意，但并未明确提及他们在被捕前为推进共谋而实施了任何后续的公开行为。然而，这并非控方的致命缺陷，原因有二。首先，MPC规定，对于共谋实施最严重的重罪（通常是一级或二级重罪），可以免除公开行为的要求。入室盗窃珠宝店几乎肯定符合此类重罪的标准，这意味着仅凭合意本身就足以构成共谋罪。其次，也是针对本题更重要的一点，该女子的驳回请求是基于外交官的豁免权，而非缺乏公开行为。题目要求我们评估的是她提出的特定法律论点的有效性。本题所考察的核心法律原则是MPC的“单边理论”，这也是A选项之所以正确的原因。外交官的个人抗辩（豁免权）并不能否定针对该女子的罪行的任何构成要件。

（选项B） 该女子是否知晓外交官的身份，与她的共谋罪责任无关。

（选项D） 尽管外交官的行为是共谋的“若无，则不”原因，但他的行为并不能免除该女子的刑事责任。相反，这些行为因满足了公开行为的要求，反而支持了对她的定罪。

教学目的：根据《Model Penal Code》(MPC)，共谋罪在以下情况成立：（1）一人怀有实施犯罪的特定意图与他人达成合意，并且（2）任何一名共谋者为推进该合意实施了公开行为。因此，MPC仅要求证明有一名有罪的参与者。

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law: Conspiracy
正确答案：A

不应批准，因为外交官的抗辩理由并未否定该罪行的任何构成要件。

核心考点：单边理论 (Unilateral Theory)

本题的关键在于题目明确指出该司法管辖区采纳了《模范刑法典》(Model Penal Code, MPC)。

在共谋罪 (Conspiracy) 的认定上，MPC 采用单边理论 (Unilateral Approach)。这意味着：

  • 共谋罪的成立仅关注被告人 (Defendant) 的主观意图和行为。
  • 只要被告人相信自己与他人达成了实施犯罪的协议，共谋即成立。
  • 另一方的情况无关紧要： 即使另一方是卧底警察（假装同意）、无行为能力人、或如本案中享有外交豁免权 (Diplomatic Immunity) 的人，都不影响被告人的刑事责任。
法律分析

1. 构成要件未被否定：
该女子具有实施入室盗窃的意图 (Intent)，并与外交官达成了协议 (Agreement)。根据 MPC，这已满足共谋罪对她的定罪要求。

2. 个人抗辩 (Personal Defense)：
外交官的豁免权是一种程序性抗辩或个人抗辩。它并不意味着“共谋”这个事实没有发生，只是法律禁止对外交官进行起诉。这种针对个人的保护伞不能延伸给该女子。

MPC vs. Common Law (普通法)
比较维度 普通法 (Common Law) 模范刑法典 (MPC)
理论基础 双边理论 (Bilateral) 单边理论 (Unilateral)
核心要求 必须有两个或以上有罪的参与者 (Two guilty minds)。 只要被告人意图达成协议即可。
一方脱罪的影响 如果一方被宣告无罪(Acquitted)，另一方通常也不能定罪。 不影响。一方的身份或抗辩不影响另一方的定罪。

为什么选项 C 错误？
选项 C ("共谋罪要求有两名有罪的参与者") 描述的是普通法 (Common Law) 的规则。如果题目没有注明适用 MPC，或者注明适用 Common Law，C 可能是正确答案。但在 MPC 规则下，这是错误的法律陈述。

💡MBE 答题技巧：
在做 Criminal Law 的题目时，务必第一时间寻找题目中是否提及 "Model Penal Code"。

如果是 MPC 辖区，涉及 Conspiracy (共谋) 时，永远记住：一个人的独角戏也可以构成共谋（只要他认为对方是真心的）。不要被同伙的疯癫、豁免权或卧底身份迷惑。

questions.question:
An art thief planned to steal a three-dimensional piece of hanging installation art from a modern art museum. Her plan involved dressing up like a museum docent, temporarily closing off the room that contained the installation art, and in the one minute it took for the security camera to visually sweep the rest of the room, hiding the installation art in a covered garbage can. Before the police or museum security would think to search a garbage can, the art thief would then disguise herself as part of the janitorial crew and remove the garbage can containing the installation art from the museum. However, on the day she planned to execute her heist, the art thief found out that the museum had recently installed hidden GPS tracking devices on all of the art pieces in the museum. The art thief decided to postpone her heist until she could figure out how to disable the GPS device and avoid getting caught. A few days later, the art thief was arrested by the police based on security footage from the museum that showed the art thief engaged in suspicious activities like stealing docent and janitorial uniforms and timing the security cameras.
Can the art thief be charged with attempted larceny of the artwork?

choices.a: No, because the element of "asportation" was not satisfied.
choices.b: No, because she abandoned the crime before it occurred.
choices.c: Yes, because she took a substantial step toward stealing the artwork.
choices.d: Yes, because attempted larceny is a general intent crime.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old student and his 14-year-old girlfriend made plans to meet in the student's apartment to have sexual intercourse, and they did so. The girlfriend later told her mother about the incident.
The student was charged with statutory rape and conspiracy to commit statutory rape. In the jurisdiction, the age of consent is 15, and the law of conspiracy is the same as at common law. The student was convicted of both charges and given consecutive sentences.
On appeal, he contends that his conspiracy conviction should be reversed.
Should the student's conviction be affirmed or reversed?

choices.a: Affirmed, because he agreed with the girlfriend to commit the crime.
choices.b: Reversed, because one cannot conspire with a person too young to consent.
choices.c: Reversed, because the crime is one that can only be committed by agreement and thus Wharton's Rule bars conspiracy liability.
choices.d: Reversed, because the girlfriend could not be a conspirator to this crime.

data.questionStem:
Q84060

An 18-year-old student and his 14-year-old girlfriend made plans to meet in the student's apartment to have sexual intercourse, and they did so. The girlfriend later told her mother about the incident.

The student was charged with statutory rape and conspiracy to commit statutory rape. In the jurisdiction, the age of consent is 15, and the law of conspiracy is the same as at common law. The student was convicted of both charges and given consecutive sentences.

On appeal, he contends that his conspiracy conviction should be reversed.

Should the student's conviction be affirmed or reversed?

一名18岁的学生与他14岁的女友计划在该学生的公寓见面并发生性关系，他们也确实这么做了。女友后来将此事告知了她的母亲。

该学生被控法定强奸罪以及共谋实施法定强奸罪。在该司法管辖区，同意年龄为15岁，且共谋法与普通法相同。该学生两项罪名均被定罪，并被判处连续服刑。

在上诉中，他主张应撤销其共谋罪的定罪。

对该学生的定罪应予以维持还是撤销？
options:
A. Affirmed, because he agreed with the girlfriend to commit the crime.
维持，因为他与女友合意实施该犯罪行为。

B. Reversed, because one cannot conspire with a person too young to consent.
撤销，因为不能与一个年龄过小而无法表示同意的人构成共谋。

C. Reversed, because the crime is one that can only be committed by agreement and thus Wharton's Rule bars conspiracy liability.
撤销，因为该罪行是一种只能通过合意才能实施的犯罪，因此Wharton's Rule排除了共谋责任的成立。

D. Reversed, because the girlfriend could not be a conspirator to this crime.
撤销，因为女友不能成为此项罪行的共谋者。
data.explanation:
Conspiracy


AgreementOvert act
Majority view (modern & MPC)Unilateral approach - at least one person specifically intends to enter agreementAt least one conspirator must commit overt act
Minority view (common law)Bilateral approach - two or more persons specifically intend to enter agreementNot required
MPC = Model Penal Code.

Common law jurisdictions follow the bilateral theory of conspiracy, which requires proof that two or more persons entered an agreement with the specific intent to accomplish a criminal act. In other words, there must be at least two guilty minds - the defendant and another conspirator. But when the agreed-upon act was criminalized to protect a certain class of persons, members of that class cannot supply a guilty mind. As a result, these protected persons cannot be convicted of the target crime or conspiracy to commit it.

Here, the 18-year-old student was convicted of conspiracy to commit statutory rape after he and his 14-year-old girlfriend agreed to have sexual intercourse. And though the student likely had a guilty mind since he specifically intended to commit this crime, the girlfriend could not supply the other guilty mind. That is because this jurisdiction's statutory-rape law is designed to protect persons under 15 years old - like the girlfriend (Choice A). As a result, there was no conspiracy and the student's conviction should be reversed.

(Choice B) A victim's consent is not a defense to conspiracy (or statutory rape) since consent does not negate an element of either crime. And regardless, persons can conspire with anyone who has the capacity to consent (ie, make reasonable judgments). So though the girlfriend was not too young to enter a conspiracy, she could not do so here because she is the type of person the statute was designed to protect.

(Choice C) Wharton's Rule bars liability for conspiracy to commit a crime that requires at least two culpable parties (eg, dueling, adultery, bigamy) and the crime is completed by only the necessary number of parties. But this rule does not apply here since the girlfriend cannot be culpable under the statutory-rape statute.

Educational objective: Common law conspiracy requires proof that at least two persons entered an agreement with the specific intent to accomplish a criminal act (ie, bilateral theory). But when the conspired act violates a statute designed to protect members of a given class, a member of that class cannot be guilty of the criminal act or conspiracy to commit it.

选项正确率统计：A选项 6%，B选项 5%，C选项 17%，D选项 70%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

共谋罪


合意公开行为
多数派观点 (现代 & MPC)单边理论 - 至少有一人明确意图达成合意至少一名共谋者必须实施公开行为
少数派观点 (普通法)双边理论 - 两人或两人以上明确意图达成合意不要求
MPC = Model Penal Code.

普通法司法管辖区遵循共谋的双边理论，该理论要求证明两人或两人以上达成合意，并具有完成犯罪行为的特定意图。换言之，必须存在至少两个有罪意图的主体——即被告和另一名共谋者。但当合意行为的刑事化是为了保护某一特定群体时，该群体的成员不能提供有罪意图。因此，这些受保护的人不能被判犯有目标罪行或共谋实施该罪行。

在本案中，这名18岁的学生因共谋实施法定强奸罪而被定罪，事发于他与14岁的女友合意发生性关系之后。尽管该学生可能有罪意图，因为他明确意图实施此项犯罪，但其女友无法提供另一个有罪意图。这是因为该司法管辖区的法定强奸罪法律旨在保护15岁以下的人——例如本案中的女友(选项 A)。因此，共谋不成立，该学生的定罪应被撤销。

(选项 B) 受害人的同意不能作为共谋罪（或法定强奸罪）的抗辩理由，因为同意并不能否定这两种罪行的任何一个构成要件。此外，无论如何，任何人都可以与具有同意能力（即，能做出合理判断）的人共谋。所以，尽管女友的年龄并未小到不能参与共谋，但在本案中她不能这样做，因为她属于该法规旨在保护的那一类人。

(选项 C) Wharton's Rule排除了对某些罪行成立共谋责任，这些罪行要求至少有两个有过错方（例如，决斗、通奸、重婚），且该罪行仅由必要数量的当事人完成。但该规则不适用于本案，因为根据法定强奸罪法规，女友不具可归责性。

教学目标：普通法上的共谋罪要求证明至少有两人达成合意，并具有完成犯罪行为的特定意图（即双边理论）。但是，当共谋的行为违反了旨在保护某一特定群体成员的法规时，该群体的成员不能被判犯有该罪行或共谋实施该罪行。

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

共谋罪与受保护群体

正确答案：D

撤销 (Reversed)，因为女友不能成为此项罪行的共谋者。

本题的核心考点在于共谋罪 (Conspiracy) 在涉及受保护群体 (Protected Class) 时的特殊规则。

⚖️ 法律规则解析

题目明确指出该司法管辖区遵循普通法 (Common Law) 的共谋规则。普通法的共谋罪适用双边理论 (Bilateral Theory)。

双边理论 (Bilateral Theory)：
共谋必须由两个或两个以上具有“有罪意图” (Guilty Mind) 的人达成合意。如果其中一方不能被定罪（例如是卧底警察或受法律保护的人），则另一方也不能单独构成共谋罪。
🛡️ 受保护群体例外原则

这是一个关键的立法意图原则 (Legislative Intent Exception)：

  • 如果一项犯罪的设立是为了保护特定群体（如未成年人、高利贷受害者），那么该群体的成员不能被视为该犯罪的共谋者或帮凶。
  • 在本案中，法定强奸罪 (Statutory Rape) 的设立是为了保护未达到同意年龄（15岁）的未成年人。

逻辑推导：

  1. 14岁的女友是法律旨在保护的受害者。
  2. 因此，她不能成为法定强奸罪的共谋者（她没有法律上的“有罪意图”）。
  3. 由于女友不能成为共谋者，剩下的只有18岁的被告一人。
  4. 根据普通法双边理论，一人无法构成共谋。

为什么不选 C (Wharton's Rule)?

这是一个极具迷惑性的选项。Wharton's Rule 通常适用于那些本质上必然需要两人参与的犯罪（如通奸 Adultery、重婚 Bigamy、乱伦 Incest、决斗 Dueling）。

规则内容：如果犯罪本身必然需要两人，除非参与人数多于犯罪构成要件所需的人数，否则不能控告共谋。

不选 C 的原因：虽然法定强奸看似需要两人，但 Wharton's Rule 适用的前提是两人都具有可归责性 (Culpability)。在本案中，因为女友是受保护方，她根本不承担刑事责任。因此，排除共谋责任的首要原因是“受保护群体原则”，而不是 Wharton's Rule。

为什么不选 A?

虽然事实上有“合意” (Agreement)，但在法定强奸案中，法律视未成年人的同意为无效。更重要的是，由于她属于受保护阶层，她的“合意”不能构成共谋罪所需的犯罪合意。

💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在 MBE 刑法题中，如果看到成年人 + 未成年人（或受害者）共同实施某种犯罪：

  1. 首先判断该法规是否旨在保护该未成年人。
  2. 如果是，该未成年人不能成为共谋者。
  3. 如果是普通法辖区（双边理论），成年被告的共谋罪名通常不成立。

questions.question:
A landlord decided to destroy his dilapidated building in order to collect the insurance money. He hired a man to burn down the building. The man broke into the building and carefully searched it to make sure no one was inside. The man failed, however, to see a person experiencing homelessness asleep in an office closet. The man started a fire. The building was destroyed, and the person experiencing homelessness died from burns a week later. Two days after the fire, the landlord filed an insurance claim in which he stated that he had no information about the cause of the fire.
The landlord is charged with felony murder of the person experiencing homelessness.
If the landlord is found guilty, it is because the death of the person experiencing homelessness occurred in connection with which felony?

choices.a: Arson.
choices.b: Burglary.
choices.c: Conspiracy.
choices.d: Fraud.

data.questionStem:
Q84038

A landlord decided to destroy his dilapidated building in order to collect the insurance money. He hired a man to burn down the building. The man broke into the building and carefully searched it to make sure no one was inside. The man failed, however, to see a vagrant asleep in an office closet. The man started a fire. The building was destroyed, and the vagrant died from burns a week later. Two days after the fire, the landlord filed an insurance claim in which he stated that he had no information about the cause of the fire.

The landlord is charged with felony murder of the vagrant.

If the landlord is found guilty, it is because the vagrant's death occurred in connection with which felony?

一名房东为了骗取保险金，决定摧毁其破旧的建筑物。他雇佣了一名男子来放火烧毁该建筑物。该男子闯入建筑物，并仔细搜查以确保里面没有人。然而，该男子未能发现一名在办公室壁橱里熟睡的流浪汉。该男子点燃了火。建筑物被烧毁，流浪汉一周后因烧伤死亡。火灾发生两天后，房东提交了保险索赔申请，声称他对火灾原因一无所知。

房东被指控犯有针对该流浪汉的 felony murder。

如果房东被判有罪，其定罪依据是该流浪汉的死亡与下列哪项重罪有关？
options:
A. Arson.
Arson.

B. Burglary.
Burglary.

C. Conspiracy.
Conspiracy.

D. Fraud.
Fraud.
data.explanation:
Accomplice liability arises when a person intentionally aids, encourages, or solicits another (principal) to commit a crime with the intent that the crime be completed. An accomplice is liable to the same extent as the principal for the encouraged crime and any crimes that occur as a natural and probable (ie, foreseeable) consequence of that crime.

Here, the landlord became an accomplice when he hired the man to burn down his building (ie, solicited arson). The landlord did not encourage the commission of felony murder - the killing of another during the commission, or attempted commission, of an inherently dangerous felony like arson. But he still could be found guilty of felony murder since the vagrant died from burns caused by that fire (foreseeable consequence of arson).

(Choice B) Burglary is an inherently dangerous felony that requires proof of a (1) trespassory entering of another's property (2) with the specific intent to commit a crime therein. Although the man intended to commit arson in the landlord's building, he did not trespass because the landlord consented to his entry (no burglary).

(Choice C) Criminal conspiracy occurs when (1) two or more persons enter an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime and (2) one of the conspirators commits an overt act in furtherance of that agreement. Although the landlord and the man conspired to commit arson, the felony murder conviction must be based on an inherently dangerous felony - not their conspiracy.

(Choice D) Fraud requires proof that the defendant made a false representation with the specific intent to permanently obtain the victim's property. But since fraud is not an inherently dangerous felony, it can never be the basis for felony murder.

Educational objective: An accomplice is someone who intentionally aids, encourages, or solicits another to commit a crime with the intent that the crime be completed. As a result, an accomplice is liable for the encouraged crime and any crimes that occur as a natural and probable consequence of that crime.



选项正确率统计：A选项 82%（正确选项），B选项 6%，C选项 7%，D选项 3%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

共犯责任产生于一人故意协助、鼓励或教唆他人（主犯）犯罪，且意图使该罪行得以完成。共犯对被鼓励的罪行以及作为该罪行自然的和可预见的（即可预见的）后果而发生的任何罪行，与主犯承担同等责任。

在本案中，房东在雇佣该男子放火烧毁其建筑物时（即教唆 arson），成为了共犯。房东没有鼓励实施 felony murder——即在实施或企图实施像 arson 这样的内在危险性重罪过程中杀害他人。但他仍可能被判犯有 felony murder，因为流浪汉死于该火灾造成的烧伤（arson 的可预见后果）。

（选项B）Burglary 是一项内在危险性重罪，需要证明（1）非法侵入他人财产，（2）并具有在其中犯罪的具体意图。虽然该男子意图在房东的建筑物内实施 arson，但他并未非法侵入，因为房东同意他进入（因此不构成 burglary）。

（选项C）Criminal conspiracy 发生于（1）两人或多人达成协议，具有实施犯罪的具体意图，且（2）其中一名共谋者为推进该协议而实施了明显行为。虽然房东和该男子共谋实施 arson，但 felony murder 的定罪必须基于一项内在危险性重罪，而非他们的 conspiracy。

（选项D）Fraud 要求证明被告作出了虚假陈述，并具有永久占有受害人财产的具体意图。但由于 fraud 并非内在危险性重罪，它永远不能成为 felony murder 的基础。

教学目的：共犯是指某人故意协助、鼓励或教唆他人犯罪，并意图使该罪行得以完成。因此，共犯对被鼓励的罪行以及作为该罪行自然的和可预见的后果而发生的任何罪行承担责任。

MBE 考题解析

Inchoate Crimes & Felony Murder

正确答案：A. Arson (纵火罪) 房东被判 Felony Murder (重罪谋杀) 的基础重罪是 Arson。
⚖️ 法律推理深度解析

1. 共犯责任 (Accomplice Liability)

房东雇佣他人烧毁建筑，构成了 Solicitation (教唆)。一旦受雇人实施了犯罪，房东作为 Accomplice (共犯/从犯)，不仅要对被教唆的罪行 (Arson) 负责，还要对该罪行产生的自然的、可预见的后果 (Natural and Probable Consequences) 负责。

2. 重罪谋杀规则 (Felony Murder Rule)

该规则规定，如果在实施内在危险性重罪 (Inherently Dangerous Felony) 的过程中导致他人死亡，被告可被控谋杀。

  • 基础重罪 (Predicate Felony)： 本案中，受雇人点火烧毁建筑的行为构成了 Arson。
  • 因果关系： 流浪汉的死亡是火灾（Arson）的直接结果。
  • 结论： 既然房东对 Arson 负有共犯责任，且死亡是 Arson 的可预见后果，那么 Arson 就是支持 Felony Murder 指控的基础重罪。
❌ 为什么其他选项是错误的？
B. Burglary (入室盗窃/夜盗)

这是本题最大的陷阱。Burglary 需要证明 "Breaking and Entering" (破门入户) 且具有 "Trespassory" (非法侵入) 的性质。因为房东拥有该建筑并同意受雇人进入，所以不存在非法侵入 (Trespass)，因此不构成 Burglary。

C. Conspiracy (共谋)

虽然房东和受雇人确实构成了 Conspiracy，但 Felony Murder 必须基于一项内在危险性重罪 (Inherently Dangerous Felony)。Conspiracy 本身通常被视为一种独立的未遂类犯罪 (Inchoate Crime)，而不是导致死亡的直接危险行为。定罪的基础是放火行为 (Arson)，而非协议行为。

D. Fraud (欺诈)

房东意图骗保确实涉及 Fraud。但是，Fraud 通常不被视为 "Inherently Dangerous Felony" (如强奸、抢劫、纵火、入室盗窃等 BARRK crimes)。因此，它不能作为 Felony Murder 的基础。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧：

1. BARRK 记忆法： 常见的支持 Felony Murder 的重罪包括 Burglary, Arson, Rape, Robbery, Kidnapping。

2. 识别 "Consent" (同意)： 在涉及 Burglary 的题目中，如果所有者同意被告进入，通常会否定 "Breaking" 或 "Trespass" 元素，从而通过排除法排除 Burglary。

3. 共犯的延伸责任： 记住共犯不仅对目标犯罪负责，还对过程中发生的可预见后果（包括意外死亡）负责。

questions.question:
A state statute provides as follows: "The maintenance of any ongoing enterprise in the nature of a betting parlor or bookmaking organization is a felony."
A prosecutor has evidence that a woman has been renting an office to a man, that the man has been using the office as a betting parlor within the meaning of the statute, and that the woman is aware of this use.
Which of the following additional pieces of evidence would be most useful to the prosecutor's effort to convict the woman as an accomplice to the man's violation of the statute?

choices.a: The man has paid the woman the rent in bills that are traceable as the proceeds of gambling activity.
choices.b: The woman charges the man considerably more in rent than she charged the preceding tenant, who used the office for legitimate activities.
choices.c: The woman has personally placed bets with the man at the office location.
choices.d: The woman was previously convicted of running a betting parlor herself on the same premises.

Q84083

A state statute provides as follows: "The maintenance of any ongoing enterprise in the nature of a betting parlor or bookmaking organization is a felony."

A prosecutor has evidence that a woman has been renting an office to a man, that the man has been using the office as a betting parlor within the meaning of the statute, and that the woman is aware of this use.

Which of the following additional pieces of evidence would be most useful to the prosecutor's effort to convict the woman as an accomplice to the man's violation of the statute?

一项州法律规定如下：“维持任何具有博彩店或博彩组织性质的持续性企业均构成重罪。”

一名检察官有证据表明，一名女子将一间办公室出租给一名男子，该男子一直将该办公室用作该法律含义范围内的博彩店，并且该女子知道此用途。

以下哪一项额外证据对于检察官努力将该女子作为该男子违反法律行为的共犯定罪最有用？
options:
A. The man has paid the woman the rent in bills that are traceable as the proceeds of gambling activity.
该男子支付给该女子的租金所用的钞票可被追溯为博彩活动的收益。

B. The woman charges the man considerably more in rent than she charged the preceding tenant, who used the office for legitimate activities.
该女子向该男子收取的租金远高于她向前一个将办公室用于合法活动的租户收取的租金。

C. The woman has personally placed bets with the man at the office location.
该女子曾亲自在该办公室与该男子下注。

D. The woman was previously convicted of running a betting parlor herself on the same premises.
该女子曾因在同一场所亲自经营博彩店而被定罪。
data.explanation:
Exclusions from accomplice liability


Member of protected classMembers of class criminal statute was designed to protect are immune from liability (eg, statutory rape)
Exempted necessary partyWhen crime requires multiple participants but criminal statute only imposes liability on one, others are immune from liability (eg, sale of narcotics)
WithdrawalNo liability if accomplice voluntarily withdraws before crime becomes unstoppable by:
  • repudiating encouragement
  • undoing or neutralizing assistance
  • notifying authorities or otherwise preventing crime
A person who aids or encourages another (ie, the principal) before or during a crime can only be convicted as an accomplice if those acts were intended to further the principal's criminal aim. Mere knowledge that the principal intends to commit a crime is not enough to prove the intent necessary for accomplice liability. But such intent can be inferred from evidence that the person has a personal stake in the commission of the crime.

Here, the woman knew that the man was using the office she rented to him as an illegal betting parlor. And her intent to aid or encourage his crime could be inferred from evidence that she personally benefits from his operation by charging him considerably higher rent than she charged the preceding tenant. Therefore, this evidence would be most useful to the prosecutor's effort to convict the woman as the man's accomplice.

(Choice A) Evidence that the man's rent payments are traceable to gambling activity would not show that the woman intended to further his crime.

(Choice C) Although maintaining a betting parlor requires more than one participant (operator and customer), the statute only imposes liability on one participant (operator). So evidence that the woman acted as a customer (an exempted necessary party) by placing bets at the office would exclude her from accomplice liability.

(Choice D) The woman's prior conviction of running a betting parlor on the same premises would be irrelevant since it would not show that she intended to help the man with his criminal enterprise.

Educational objective: An accomplice must aid or encourage the principal with the intent to further the principal's criminal aim. Such intent can be inferred when the accomplice has a personal stake in the crime being committed.

选项正确率统计：A选项 6%，B选项 55%（正确选项），C选项 34%，D选项 3%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

共犯责任的除外情形


受保护阶层成员刑事法律旨在保护的阶层成员免于承担责任（例如，statutory rape）
被豁免的必要参与方当犯罪需要多名参与者，但刑事法律仅对其中一人施加责任时，其他人免于承担责任（例如，销售麻醉品）
退出如果共犯在犯罪变得无法制止之前通过以下方式自愿退出，则不承担责任：
  • 放弃教唆
  • 撤销或抵消帮助
  • 通知当局或以其他方式阻止犯罪
一个人在犯罪之前或期间帮助或教唆他人（即主犯），只有当这些行为意图是为促进主犯的犯罪目的时，才能作为共犯被定罪。仅仅知道主犯意图犯罪，并不足以证明共犯责任所必需的意图。但这种意图可以被推断出来，如果证据显示该人在犯罪的实施中具有个人利害关系。

在本案中，该女子知道该男子将她租给他的办公室用作非法博彩店。而她帮助或教唆其犯罪的意图，可以从她通过向该男子收取远高于前租户的租金从而从其经营中个人获益的证据中推断出来。因此，这项证据对于检察官努力将该女子作为该男子的共犯定罪最有用。

(选项 A) 该男子的租金可追溯到博彩活动的证据，并不能表明该女子意图促进其犯罪。

(选项 C) 尽管维持一家博彩店需要多于一名参与者（经营者和顾客），但该法律仅对一名参与者（经营者）施加责任。所以，证明该女子通过在办公室下注而充当顾客（一个被豁免的必要参与方）的证据，将会把她从共犯责任中排除。

(选项 D) 该女子先前因在同一场所经营博彩店而被定罪的记录是不相关的，因为它不能表明她意图帮助该男子进行他的犯罪企业。

教学目的：共犯必须帮助或教唆主犯，并且具有促进主犯犯罪目的的意图。当共犯在正在实施的犯罪中具有个人利害关系时，这种意图可以被推断出来。

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

刑法：共犯责任与意图
✅ 正确答案：选项 B

该女子向该男子收取的租金远高于她向前一个将办公室用于合法活动的租户收取的租金。

核心法律原则

本题考察的是共犯责任 (Accomplice Liability) 中的核心要素：犯罪意图 (Mens Rea)。

根据普通法和大多数司法管辖区的规定，要成为共犯，被告必须具备双重意图：

  1. 意图协助主犯的行为；
  2. 意图促进犯罪的完成 (Intent that the crime be committed)。
深度解析：知情 vs. 意图

这是 MBE 刑法部分的一个经典考点，通常被称为 "Supplier of Goods or Services" (商品或服务提供者) 问题。

一般规则：单纯知情不足以定罪
仅仅知道他人将利用你提供的服务（如出租房屋、出售电话服务）进行犯罪，通常不足以证明共犯所需的“意图”。
Mere knowledge is generally insufficient for accomplice liability.

例外：利益相关 (Stake in the Venture)
如果服务提供者在犯罪活动中有“个人利害关系” (Stake in the Venture)，法院允许陪审团从中推断出犯罪意图。

为什么选项 B 是最强证据？

当房东收取的租金远高于市场价（或前任合法租户的价格）时，这表明：

  • 房东正在收取“风险溢价”。
  • 房东的超额利润直接依赖于非法生意的成功（如果是合法生意，租户不会支付这种高价）。

这种超额收费确立了房东在犯罪中的利益相关性，从而可以推断她不仅“知道”，而且“希望”该非法博彩店继续经营，以维持她的高额租金收入。

为什么其他选项不够好？
选项 A (钞票来源)：
这仅证明她收到了钱，且钱来自赌博。但这只能证明“知情” (Knowledge)，无法证明她为了获取利益而积极希望犯罪成功。卖三明治给毒贩并收到毒资，并不让你成为贩毒共犯。
选项 C (亲自下注)：
这会让该女子成为“顾客”。根据惠顿规则 (Wharton's Rule) 或相关成文法解释，如果法律旨在惩罚经营者，通常会将“必要的参与方” (Necessary Parties)（如购买违禁品的顾客、赌客）排除在共犯责任之外。作为顾客下注不能证明她作为房东协助经营的意图。
选项 D (前科记录)：
先前的定罪属于品格证据 (Character Evidence)。虽然它可能显示该女子熟悉博彩业，但它不能直接证明她在本次特定交易中意图协助该男子犯罪。且此类证据通常因偏见过大而被排除。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

遇到“供应商/房东 + 犯罪客户”的题目时，请寻找以下能证明意图 (Intent) 的加分项（参考 People v. Lauria 案）：

  1. 在非法商品中占有股份/分红（Stake in the venture，如本题的高额租金）。
  2. 该服务除了犯罪外没有合法用途。
  3. 交易量巨大，与合法需求不成比例。

如果没有这些因素，仅凭“知情”通常选“无罪”。

questions.question:
A man was engaged to marry a woman. One evening, the man became enraged at the comments of the woman's eight-year-old daughter, who was complaining, in her usual fashion, that she did not want her mother to marry the man. The man, who had had too much to drink, began beating the daughter. The daughter suffered some bruises and a broken arm. The woman took her daughter to the hospital, and the police were notified by the hospital staff.
The man was indicted for felony child abuse. He pleaded with the woman to forgive him and to run away with him. She agreed. They moved out of state and took the daughter with them. Without the testimony of the child, the prosecution was forced to dismiss the case. Some time later, the woman returned for a visit with her family and was arrested and indicted as an accessory after the fact to child abuse.
At the woman's trial, how should the court proceed?

choices.a: Dismiss the charge, because the evidence shows that any aid the woman rendered occurred after the crime was completed.
choices.b: Dismiss the charge, because the man had not been convicted.
choices.c: Submit the case to the jury, on an instruction to convict only if the woman knew the man had been indicted.
choices.d: Submit the case to the jury, on an instruction to convict only if the woman's purpose in moving was to help the man avoid conviction.

一名男子与一名女子订婚。一天晚上，该女子八岁的女儿像往常一样抱怨说，她不希望母亲嫁给该男子。该男子听后勃然大怒。该男子因饮酒过量，开始殴打该女孩。女孩身上多处瘀伤，手臂骨折。女子将女儿送往医院，医院工作人员通知了警方。

该男子因重罪虐待儿童罪被起诉。他恳求女子原谅他并与他一同私奔。女子同意了。他们带着女儿搬离了本州。由于没有女孩的证词，检方被迫撤销了此案。一段时间后，该女子回家探亲时被逮捕，并被控为虐待儿童罪的事后从犯。

在对该女子的审判中，法院应如何处理？
options:
A. Dismiss the charge, because the evidence shows that any aid the woman rendered occurred after the crime was completed.
驳回指控，因为证据显示该女子提供的任何帮助都发生在该罪行完成后。

B. Dismiss the charge, because the man had not been convicted.
驳回指控，因为该男子尚未被定罪。

C. Submit the case to the jury, on an instruction to convict only if the woman knew the man had been indicted.
将案件提交给陪审团，并指示只有在该女子知道该男子已被起诉的情况下才能定罪。

D. Submit the case to the jury, on an instruction to convict only if the woman's purpose in moving was to help the man avoid conviction.
将案件提交给陪审团，并指示只有在该女子搬家的目的是为了帮助该男子逃避定罪的情况下才能定罪。
data.explanation:
Parties to a crime


Modern viewCommon lawDefinitionLiability
PrincipalPrincipal (first degree)Performs criminal act with requisite intent or uses innocent agent to commit criminal actTarget & foreseeable crimes
AccomplicePrincipal (second degree)Present at crime & aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crimeTarget & foreseeable crimes
AccompliceAccessory before the fact Not present at crime but aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crimeTarget & foreseeable crimes
Accessory after the factAccessory after the factKnows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or convictionIndependent crime
Common law liability requires conviction of principal.

A person is an accessory after the fact if he/she:
  • knew that the principal had committed a felony
  • aided or assisted the principal after the felony was complete and
  • did so for the purpose of helping the principal avoid apprehension or conviction.


Although the accessory after the fact is not liable for the principal's crime, the accessory is liable for a separate crime - often "harboring a fugitive" or "obstructing justice".

Here, the man was indicted for felony child abuse after beating the woman's daughter. Although the woman was aware of this crime, she moved out of state with the man and her daughter. This move helped the man avoid conviction since the daughter's unavailability to testify forced the state to dismiss his case. But the jury should only convict the woman as an accessory after the fact if her purpose in moving was to help the man avoid conviction.

(Choice A) The evidence that the woman aided the man after the crime was completed supports her liability as an accessory after the fact - not a dismissal of the charge.

(Choice B) A person can be convicted as an accessory after the fact even if the principal has not been prosecuted for, or convicted of, the completed felony.

(Choice C) An accessory after the fact must know that the principal has committed a felony but need not know that the principal has been indicted for that crime.

Educational objective: An accessory after the fact (1) knows that the principal has committed a felony, (2) aids or assists the principal after the felony is complete, and (3) does so to help the principal avoid apprehension or conviction.

选项正确率统计：A选项 5%，B选项 8%，C选项 7%，D选项 78%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

犯罪参与人


现代观点普通法定义责任
主犯 (Principal)主犯（一级）(Principal (first degree))以必要的犯意实施犯罪行为，或利用无辜的代理人实施犯罪行为目标罪行和可预见的罪行
共犯 (Accomplice)主犯（二级）(Principal (second degree))在犯罪现场，并以主犯实施犯罪的意图，帮助/鼓励主犯目标罪行和可预见的罪行
共犯 (Accomplice)事前从犯 (Accessory before the fact) 不在犯罪现场，但以主犯实施犯罪的意图，帮助/鼓励主犯目标罪行和可预见的罪行
事后从犯 (Accessory after the fact)事后从犯 (Accessory after the fact)知道主犯犯下重罪，并帮助主犯逃避逮捕或定罪独立犯罪
普通法下的责任要求主犯已被定罪。

一个人构成事后从犯 (accessory after the fact)，如果他/她：
  • 知道主犯已犯下重罪
  • 在重罪完成后帮助或协助了主犯，并且
  • 其目的是为了帮助主犯逃避逮捕或定罪。


尽管事后从犯不对主犯的罪行负责，但该从犯对一项独立的罪行负责——通常是“窝藏逃犯罪”或“妨害司法罪”。

在本案中，该男子在殴打该女子的女儿后，因重罪虐待儿童罪被起诉。尽管该女子知道这一罪行，但她还是与该男子和她的女儿搬离了本州。这一举动帮助该男子逃避了定罪，因为女儿无法出庭作证，迫使州政府撤销了他的案件。但是，只有在该女子搬家的目的是帮助该男子逃避定罪的情况下，陪审团才应判定其为事后从犯。

(选项 A) 证据表明该女子在罪行完成后帮助了该男子，这支持了她作为事后从犯的责任——而不是驳回指控。

(选项 B) 即使主犯尚未因已完成的重罪被起诉或定罪，一个人也可以被判定为事后从犯。

(选项 C) 事后从犯必须知道主犯实施了一项重罪，但不必知道主犯已因此罪行被起诉。

教学目的：事后从犯 (accessory after the fact) 的构成要件为 (1) 知道主犯已犯下重罪，(2) 在重罪完成后帮助或协助主犯，以及 (3) 这么做的目的是帮助主犯逃避逮捕或定罪。

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law: Parties to a Crime
核心考点：事后从犯 (Accessory After the Fact)

本题考察的是认定事后从犯所需的“特定意图” (Specific Intent)。仅仅提供帮助是不够的，必须是为了阻碍正义。

✅ 正确答案解析 (选项 D)

法院应指示陪审团：只有当该女子搬家的目的是为了帮助该男子逃避定罪时，才能将其定罪。

法律依据：

构成 Accessory After the Fact 需要满足以下三个要素：

  1. 重罪已完成 (Completed Felony)： 主犯必须已经实施了重罪。
  2. 明知 (Knowledge)： 被告必须知道主犯实施了该重罪。
  3. 特定意图的协助 (Assistance with Specific Intent)： 被告必须亲自协助主犯，且目的是为了防止主犯被逮捕、审判或定罪。

本案关键：虽然女子带孩子搬家客观上导致了案件撤销（因为没有证人），但这并不自动构成犯罪。陪审团必须认定她的主观意图 (Mens Rea) 是为了帮助男子逃避法律制裁，而不是出于其他原因（如为了爱情、为了开始新生活等）。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A：驳回指控，因为帮助发生在罪行完成后

这是概念混淆。如果在罪行发生前或发生时提供帮助，那是 Accomplice（共犯）。正是因为帮助发生在罪行完成后，才构成了“事后从犯”。这是定罪的理由，而非驳回的理由。

选项 B：驳回指控，因为男子未被定罪

这是普通法（Common Law）的旧规则。现代法律视“事后从犯”为一项独立的犯罪 (Independent Crime)，通常称为妨碍司法公正或窝藏罪。即使主犯（Principal）逃脱或未被定罪，事后从犯依然可以被单独起诉。

选项 C：需知道男子已被起诉 (Indicted)

法律只要求从犯知道主犯实施了重罪 (Committed a felony)，并不要求知道具体的法律程序状态（如是否已被正式起诉）。女子目睹了虐待并送医，她显然知道犯罪事实。

💡 MBE 答题技巧

在刑法题目中，当涉及到从犯 (Parties to a crime) 时，请务必检查心理状态 (Mens Rea)：

  • 仅仅“在场”或“知情”通常不足以定罪。
  • 对于事后从犯，必须寻找“为了帮助逃避抓捕/定罪”这一特定目的。
  • 如果题目中的行为（如搬家）可能有多种解释，正确答案通常会要求陪审团确认其犯罪意图。

questions.question:
A man decided to rob a bank to pay off his crippling loan debt, so he purchased a gun, a mask, and some duffel bags. The man then told his friend that he had decided to rob a local bank and was going to scope it out the next day. As planned, the man went inside the local bank to look around. After surveilling the bank, he decided not to go through with robbing the bank because a bank in the neighboring city had fewer cameras. Unbeknownst to the man, the friend had called the police to inform them of the man's plan. As the man was walking back to his car, he was arrested by the police.
Of what crime, if any, may the man be properly convicted?

choices.a: Attempted robbery, because he still intended to rob the neighboring bank.
choices.b: No crime, because he voluntarily withdrew from the robbery.
choices.c: No crime, because his conduct did not exceed mere preparation.
choices.d: Robbery, because he committed an act in furtherance of that crime.

Q84070

A man decided to rob a bank to pay off his crippling loan debt, so he purchased a gun, a mask, and some duffel bags. The man then told his friend that he had decided to rob a local bank and was going to scope it out the next day. As planned, the man went inside the local bank to look around. After surveilling the bank, he decided not to go through with robbing the bank because a bank in the neighboring city had fewer cameras. Unbeknownst to the man, the friend had called the police to inform them of the man's plan. As the man was walking back to his car, he was arrested by the police.

In a jurisdiction that follows the common law of attempt, of what crime, if any, may the man be properly convicted?

一名男子为偿还其沉重的贷款债务，决定抢劫一家银行，因此他购买了一把枪、一个面具和几个行李袋。该男子随后告诉他的朋友，他已决定抢劫一家本地银行，并打算第二天去踩点。按照计划，该男子进入本地银行进行查看。在勘查了该银行后，他决定放弃抢劫，因为邻近城市的一家银行摄像头更少。该男子不知情的是，他的朋友已经报警，将该男子的计划告知了警方。在该男子走回他的车时，他被警察逮捕了。

在一个遵循普通法关于犯罪未遂规定的司法管辖区，该男子可能被判定犯有何种罪行（如有）？
options:
A. No crime, because his conduct did not exceed mere preparation.
不构成犯罪，因为他的行为没有超出单纯的预备阶段。

B. No crime, because he voluntarily withdrew from the robbery.
不构成犯罪，因为他自愿地中止了抢劫行为。

C. Attempted robbery, because he still intended to rob the neighboring bank.
抢劫未遂罪，因为他仍打算抢劫邻近城市的银行。

D. Robbery, because he committed an overt act in furtherance of that crime.
抢劫罪，因为他为促进该犯罪实施了明显行为。
data.explanation:
Tests for Overt Act in Attempt


Dangerous Proximity Test (Common Law)
Defendant's acts must be 'dangerously close' to completing the crime. Focuses on what remains to be done.
Substantial Step Test (Majority & MPC)
Defendant's conduct exceeds mere preparation & strongly corroborates criminal intent. Focuses on what has already been done.
Attempt occurs when a defendant has the specific intent to commit a crime and performs an overt act in furtherance of that crime. The key issue is what constitutes a sufficient overt act. Under the traditional common law, the defendant's acts must go beyond mere preparation and be in 'dangerous proximity' to the completion of the crime. This test focuses on how much the defendant has left to do. Acts are generally not considered dangerously proximate if they are still remote in time or place from the final act needed to complete the crime.

Here, while the man had the specific intent to rob the bank and took preparatory steps (buying supplies, surveilling the location), his actions did not reach the point of dangerous proximity. He was still in the reconnaissance phase and had not yet begun the actual commission of the robbery (e.g., approaching the teller with the gun). Under the strict common law standard, his conduct would be considered mere preparation.

(Choice A) This is the correct answer. In a common law jurisdiction using the dangerous proximity test, the man's actions, including surveilling the bank, would not be considered sufficient to constitute the crime of attempt. His conduct had not yet placed him dangerously close to the consummation of the robbery.

(Choice C) This would be the correct answer in a jurisdiction following the modern 'substantial step' test (the majority/MPC rule). Surveilling the target is a classic example of a substantial step. However, this jurisdiction follows the stricter common law test, under which his actions are insufficient.

(Choice B) This is incorrect because the issue of abandonment or withdrawal is only relevant if the crime of attempt has already been committed. Since the man's actions never crossed the threshold from preparation to attempt under the common law, the reason for his desistance is legally irrelevant to the attempt charge.

(Choice D) This is incorrect. The man did not complete the robbery, so he cannot be convicted of the completed crime.

Educational objective: Under the common law 'dangerous proximity' test for attempt, the defendant's acts must be very close to the actual completion of the crime. Actions that would be considered a 'substantial step' under the MPC, such as surveillance, may still be considered 'mere preparation' under the common law.

犯罪未遂中“明显行为”的检验标准


危险接近测试 (普通法)
被告人的行为必须“危险地接近”完成犯罪。该标准关注还剩下多少步骤未完成。
重大步骤测试 (多数州 & MPC)
被告人的行为超出了单纯的预备阶段，并有力地证实了其犯罪意图。该标准关注已经完成了哪些步骤。
犯罪未遂发生于被告人具有实施犯罪的特定意图，并为促进该犯罪而实施了明显行为。关键问题在于何种行为构成了一个充分的“明显行为”。在传统普通法下，被告人的行为必须超越单纯的预备阶段，并达到与完成犯罪“危险接近”（dangerous proximity）的程度。该测试关注的是被告人还有多少步骤没有完成。如果行为在时间或地点上与完成犯罪所需的最后一步还相距甚远，通常不被认为是危险接近。

在本案中，尽管该男子有抢劫银行的特定意图，并采取了预备步骤（购买物资、勘查地点），但他的行为并未达到危险接近的程度。他仍处于侦察阶段，尚未开始实施实际的抢劫行为（例如，持枪接近出纳员）。在严格的普通法标准下，他的行为将被视为单纯的预备。

(选项A) 这是正确答案。在一个采用“危险接近测试”的普通法司法管辖区，该男子的行为，包括勘查银行，不足以构成犯罪未遂。他的行为尚未使其危险地接近抢劫罪的完成。

(选项C) 在一个遵循现代“重大步骤测试”（多数州/MPC规则）的司法管辖区，这将是正确答案。勘查目标是“重大步骤”的一个典型例子。然而，本题的司法管辖区遵循的是更严格的普通法测试，据此，他的行为是不充分的。

(选项B) 这是不正确的，因为只有在犯罪未遂已经成立的情况下，中止或放弃的问题才具有相关性。由于在普通法下，该男子的行为从未跨越从预备到未遂的门槛，因此他停止犯罪的原因对于未遂指控在法律上是无关紧要的。

(选项D) 这是不正确的。该男子并未完成抢劫，因此不能被判定犯有既遂罪。

教学目标：在普通法关于犯罪未遂的“危险接近测试”下，被告人的行为必须非常接近犯罪的实际完成。某些在MPC下会被认为是“重大步骤”的行为，如监视，在普通法下仍可能被视为“单纯的预备”。

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law: Attempt (Common Law)
正确答案：A 不构成犯罪，因为他的行为没有超出单纯的预备阶段。
(No crime, because his conduct did not exceed mere preparation.)
核心考点：未遂罪的认定标准

本题的关键在于区分普通法 (Common Law) 与 模范刑法典 (MPC) 对“犯罪未遂” (Attempt) 的不同认定标准。

犯罪未遂通常包含两个要素：

  1. 实施犯罪的特定意图 (Specific Intent)。
  2. 为实施该犯罪而进行的明显行为 (Overt Act)。

本题考察的是第2点：什么算作“明显行为”？

标准 普通法 (Common Law)
*本题考点		 现代法/MPC (Modern)
测试名称 Dangerous Proximity Test
(危险接近测试)		 Substantial Step Test
(重大步骤测试)
关注点 关注还剩下多少步骤未完成。行为必须在物理上或时间上非常接近犯罪既遂。 关注已经完成了哪些步骤。只要行为有力地佐证了犯罪意图即可。
踩点行为
(Scoping out)		 通常视为单纯预备 (Mere Preparation)，不构成未遂。 通常视为重大步骤，构成未遂。
案情分析
购买工具 (Buying gear)
单纯预备 (Mere Preparation)
踩点/侦查 (Surveillance)
被告人在此停止。在普通法下，这仍属于准备工作，尚未达到“危险接近”实际抢劫的程度（如掏枪、递纸条）。
普通法未遂门槛
需极度接近完成 (Dangerous Proximity)。
既遂 (Completion)

由于题目明确指出适用普通法 (Common Law)，被告人的行为（买枪、踩点）虽然有犯罪意图，但在物理距离和时间上尚未达到“危险接近”抢劫成功的程度。他还有大把机会放弃（Locus Poenitentiae）。因此，这只是“单纯预备”，不构成犯罪。

干扰项解析
  • 选项 B (Withdrawal/Abandonment): 这是一个常见的陷阱。只有当行为已经构成“未遂”时，才讨论是否可以因“中止”而免责。既然在普通法下他甚至还没构成未遂，中止抗辩就无从谈起。此外，普通法通常不允许中止作为未遂的抗辩。
  • 选项 C (Attempted Robbery): 这是在 MPC 管辖区下的正确答案。踩点 (Scoping out) 在 MPC 下属于“重大步骤” (Substantial Step)。但题目限定了普通法。
  • 选项 D (Robbery): 抢劫罪要求实际的取财行为，显然未发生。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧：
做 Attempt 题目时，第一步必须看清题目设定的司法管辖区 (Jurisdiction)：

1. 如果是 Common Law ➝ 选标准更严的“危险接近”，踩点通常无罪。
2. 如果是 MPC / Majority ➝ 选标准较宽的“重大步骤”，踩点通常有罪。

如果题目未说明，通常默认适用 MPC/Modern 规则，但本题明确指出了 Common Law，这是解题的唯一线索。

questions.question:
A woman who wanted to rob a bank offered to pay her friend one-third of the money she stole if the friend would drive the getaway car to be used in the robbery. The friend agreed but made the woman promise not to hurt anyone during the robbery.
The woman then drove to a sporting goods store, where she explained to the store owner that she needed a small firearm for use in a bank robbery. The store owner responded that he would charge extra because the woman was so unwise as to confide her unlawful plans for using the weapon, and he sold her a handgun at four times the regular price.
During the robbery, the woman used the gun to threaten a bank teller, who handed over money. The gun discharged by accident and killed a bank customer. The friend drove the woman away from the bank.
In addition to the woman, who could properly be convicted of murder in the death of the customer at common law?

choices.a: Both the friend and the store owner.
choices.b: Neither the friend nor the store owner.
choices.c: Only the friend.
choices.d: Only the store owner.

Q84050

A woman who wanted to rob a bank offered to pay her friend one-third of the money she stole if the friend would drive the getaway car to be used in the robbery. The friend agreed but made the woman promise not to hurt anyone during the robbery.

The woman then drove to a sporting goods store, where she explained to the store owner that she needed a small firearm for use in a bank robbery. The store owner responded that he would charge extra because the woman was so unwise as to confide her unlawful plans for using the weapon, and he sold her a handgun at four times the regular price.

During the robbery, the woman used the gun to threaten a bank teller, who handed over money. The gun discharged by accident and killed a bank customer. The friend drove the woman away from the bank.

In addition to the woman, who could properly be convicted of murder in the death of the customer at common law?

一名想抢劫银行的女子向其朋友提议，如果朋友愿意驾驶抢劫时使用的逃逸车辆，她将支付所盗金额的三分之一作为报酬。朋友同意了，但让该女子承诺在抢劫过程中不伤害任何人。

随后，该女子驾车前往一家体育用品商店，向店主解释说她需要一把小型枪支用于银行抢劫。店主回应称，由于该女子如此不明智地吐露了她使用武器的非法计划，他要收取额外费用，并以四倍于正常价格的价格向她出售了一把手枪。

在抢劫过程中，该女子用枪威胁一名银行出纳员，后者交出了钱款。枪支意外走火，杀死了一名银行顾客。朋友驾车将该女子送离了银行。

根据普通法(common law)，除了该女子外，谁还可能因该顾客的死亡而被适当定为谋杀罪？
options:
A. Both the friend and the store owner.
朋友和店主两人均是。

B. Neither the friend nor the store owner.
朋友和店主两人均不是。

C. Only the friend.
仅朋友一人。

D. Only the store owner.
仅店主一人。
data.explanation:
Parties to a crime


Modern viewCommon lawDefinitionLiability
PrincipalPrincipal (first degree)Performs criminal act with requisite intent or uses innocent agent to commit criminal actTarget & foreseeable crimes
AccomplicePrincipal (second degree)Present at crime & aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crimeTarget & foreseeable crimes
AccompliceAccessory before the fact Not present at crime but aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crimeTarget & foreseeable crimes
Accessory after the factAccessory after the factKnows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or convictionIndependent crime
Common law liability requires conviction of principal.

Accomplice liability extends to anyone who intentionally aids or encourages a principal before or during the commission of a crime with the specific intent that the principal commit the encouraged crime.

Common law jurisdictions (as seen here) divide accomplices into two categories - those who were present for the crime (principals in the second degree) and those who were not (accessories before the fact). But accomplices under either category are liable to the same extent as the principal for the encouraged crime and any crimes that occurred as a natural and probable (ie, foreseeable) consequence of that crime.

Here, the woman (principal in the first degree) can be convicted of murder because she killed a customer in the course of a bank robbery. The friend intentionally aided in that robbery by driving the woman away from the bank after the robbery was completed - as they previously agreed. And since the killing was a foreseeable consequence of the robbery, the friend (who was at the crime) can be convicted of murder as a principal in the second degree (Choices B & D).

The store owner's intent to aid in the woman's robbery cannot be inferred from his decision to sell her a gun after learning of her criminal plan. But it can be inferred from his sale of the gun at four times the regular price since the sale shows that the store owner has an interest in the outcome of criminal venture. And since it was foreseeable that the gun would be used to kill someone during the robbery, the store owner (who was not at the crime) can be convicted of murder as an accessory before the fact (Choice C).

Educational objective: Principals in the second degree (accomplices at the crime) and accessories before the fact (accomplices not at the crime) are liable at common law for:
  • any crimes that they encouraged a principal in the first degree to commit and
  • any crimes that occurred as a foreseeable consequence of the encouraged crime.


选项正确率统计：A选项 65%（正确选项），B选项 2%，C选项 27%，D选项 4%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

犯罪参与人


现代观点普通法(Common law)定义责任
正犯(Principal)一级正犯(Principal (first degree))具有必要犯意并实施犯罪行为，或利用无辜代理人实施犯罪行为目标罪行及可预见的罪行
共犯(Accomplice)二级正犯(Principal (second degree))在犯罪现场，并怀有协助/鼓励正犯犯罪的意图目标罪行及可预见的罪行
共犯(Accomplice)事前从犯(Accessory before the fact) 不在犯罪现场，但怀有协助/鼓励正犯犯罪的意图目标罪行及可预见的罪行
事后从犯(Accessory after the fact)事后从犯(Accessory after the fact)明知正犯已犯下重罪，并帮助正犯逃避逮捕或定罪独立的罪行
普通法下的责任要求正犯已被定罪。

共犯责任(Accomplice liability)适用于任何在犯罪实施前或实施中，故意协助或鼓励正犯，并具有希望正犯实施所鼓励之罪行的特定意图的人。

在普通法司法管辖区（如本案所示），共犯分为两类——在犯罪时在场的（二级正犯）和不在场的（事前从犯）。但无论是哪一类的共犯，其对所鼓励的罪行以及作为该罪行自然且可能（即可预见的）后果而发生的任何罪行，都与正犯承担同等责任。

在本案中，该女子（一级正犯）可被判谋杀罪，因为她在抢劫银行的过程中杀死了一名顾客。朋友根据他们之前的约定，在抢劫完成后驾车将该女子送离银行，从而故意协助了该抢劫行为。由于杀人是抢劫的可预见后果，因此该朋友（在犯罪现场）可以作为二级正犯被判谋杀罪（因此选项B和D不正确）。

店主协助该女子抢劫的意图，不能仅从其得知她的犯罪计划后决定卖枪给她的行为中推断出来。但是，可以从他以四倍正常价格出售枪支的行为中推断出此意图，因为该销售行为表明店主在这起犯罪事业的结果中拥有利益。并且，由于可以预见到枪支在抢劫中会被用来杀人，该店主（不在犯罪现场）可以作为事前从犯被判谋杀罪（因此选项C不正确）。

教学目标：在普通法下，二级正犯（在犯罪现场的共犯）和事前从犯（不在犯罪现场的共犯）对以下行为承担责任：
  • 他们鼓励一级正犯实施的任何罪行，以及
  • 作为所鼓励罪行的可预见后果而发生的任何罪行。

MBE 考点解析

共犯责任与重罪谋杀
Accomplice Liability & Felony Murder

本题考查的是普通法（Common Law）下的共犯分类以及共犯对不可预见后果的责任范围。正确答案是 A (Both the friend and the store owner)。

核心原则：
共犯（Accomplice）不仅对目标犯罪（Target Crime）负责，还对正犯在实施犯罪过程中犯下的所有自然且可能（Natural and Probable）的罪行负责。

1. 朋友的责任分析

朋友在普通法下属于 Principal in the Second Degree（二级正犯）。

  • 定义：在犯罪现场（Present）并协助或鼓励犯罪的人。虽然他在车里，但在法律上被视为“建设性在场”（Constructively Present）。
  • 抗辩无效：朋友辩称他要求“不要伤害任何人”。但在法律上，持枪抢劫银行本质上是危险的。
  • 结论：顾客的死亡是持枪抢劫的可预见后果（Foreseeable Consequence）。根据重罪谋杀规则（Felony Murder Rule），所有参与抢劫的共犯都对抢劫过程中的死亡负责，无论其主观意愿如何。

2. 店主的责任分析

店主在普通法下属于 Accessory Before the Fact（事前从犯）。

  • 定义：不在犯罪现场，但在犯罪前提供协助、建议或鼓励的人。
  • 关键考点 - 意图（Intent）：通常，仅仅知道买家要犯罪而出售商品（Mere Knowledge）不足以构成共犯意图。
    但是，本题中店主以四倍价格出售。
  • 利益关联（Stake in the Venture）：高价出售表明店主不仅“知情”，而且通过从非法用途中获利，与犯罪建立了利益关联。这足以推断出他具有协助犯罪的特定意图（Specific Intent）。
  • 结论：店主协助了抢劫，且杀人是持枪抢劫的可预见后果，因此他也对谋杀负责。
⚖️ 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在 MBE 刑法题中，注意区分知情（Knowledge）与意图（Intent）：

  • 如果店主只是按原价卖枪，即使知道用途，通常也不承担共犯责任（除非涉及极度严重的重罪）。
  • 一旦店主加价（Charge Extra），他就有了“Stake in the venture”（风险投资/分一杯羹），这直接确立了共犯责任。

3. 普通法下的分类总结

虽然现代法律（如 MPC）已废除这些区分，但 MBE 经常考查 Common Law 的分类：

  • Principal in the 1st Degree: 实施犯罪的人（女子）。
  • Principal in the 2nd Degree: 在场协助的人（朋友）。
  • Accessory Before the Fact: 不在场但事前协助的人（店主）。
  • Accessory After the Fact: 事后帮助逃避抓捕的人（本题未涉及，且通常只对妨碍司法负责，不对原罪负责）。

注意：前三者对所犯下的重罪（谋杀）承担同等责任。

一名面临财务困难的艺术家请求她在美术馆担任保安的朋友帮助她，让朋友不要锁上博物馆的仓库，以便她可以偷走画作并用赝品替换。该艺术家表示，她会用她利润的一半来酬谢这位朋友。这位朋友表示同意，但事实上他无权进入博物馆的仓库，也无意不锁仓库。当天晚些时候，他向警方通报了她的计划。该艺术家立即被捕。

适用的司法管辖区对所有相关规则均遵循普通法。

该艺术家犯了以下哪项罪行？
options:
A. Attempted larceny.
盗窃未遂罪。

B. Bribery.
贿赂罪。

C. Conspiracy.
共谋罪。

D. Solicitation.
教唆罪。
data.explanation:
Defenses unique to solicitation


ImpossibilityLegal - when solicited act would not be criminal if completed Factual - no defense
Withdrawal / RenunciationMajority/common law - no defense Minority/MPC - when solicitor voluntarily renounces & thwarts commission of solicited crime
Exemption from solicited crimeNot guilty of solicited crime if legislature intended to protect solicitor
MPC = Model Penal Code

Solicitation is an inchoate crime that occurs when a person:
  • entices, encourages, requests, or commands another to commit a crime (eg, requests another to act as an accomplice to larceny)
  • with the specific intent that the solicited crime be committed.
Solicitation is complete once these elements are met. This is true regardless of whether the solicited party agrees to commit the crime or takes any step toward doing so. As a result, factual impossibility - eg, the solicited party's inability or lack of intent to commit the offense - is not a defense.

Here, the crime of solicitation was committed the moment the artist asked the friend to help her commit larceny. Therefore, the artist committed solicitation even though the friend did not have the ability or intent to open the warehouse or leave it unlocked.

(Choice A) Attempt occurs when the defendant (1) had the specific intent to commit a crime, (2) performed an overt act in furtherance of the crime, but (3) did not complete it. Under the common law dangerous-proximity test, the overt act must bring the defendant sufficiently close to completing the crime. But here, the artist was arrested before she could take an action that brought her close to stealing the paintings.

(Choice B) Common law bribery is the corrupt payment of something of value for the purpose of influencing the action of a public official in the discharge of his/her public or legal duties. A security guard is not a public official, so the artist did not commit bribery.

(Choice C) The common law, bilateral approach to conspiracy requires proof of at least two guilty minds. As a result, a defendant could not be convicted if the other conspirator feigned agreement (as seen here).

Educational objective: Solicitation is complete once a person (1) entices, encourages, requests, or commands another to commit a crime (2) with the specific intent that the solicited crime be committed. Factual impossibility is not a defense to solicitation.

选项正确率统计：A选项 18%，B选项 2%，C选项 13%，D选项 65%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

教唆罪的特有抗辩理由


不能犯 (Impossibility)法律上 - 如果被教唆的行为完成时并不构成犯罪；事实上 - 无抗辩理由
撤回/放弃 (Withdrawal / Renunciation)多数/普通法 - 无抗辩理由；少数/MPC - 当教唆者自愿放弃并阻止被教唆的犯罪得逞时
免于被教唆的罪行 (Exemption from solicited crime)如果立法机关旨在保护教唆者，则不构成被教唆的罪行
MPC = Model Penal Code

教唆罪 (Solicitation) 是一种未遂罪，指当一个人：
  • 引诱、鼓励、请求或命令他人犯罪（例如，请求他人充当盗窃罪的共犯）
  • 具有希望被教唆的罪行得以实施的特定意图。
一旦满足这些要素，教唆罪即告成立。无论被教唆方是否同意犯罪或采取任何步骤实施犯罪，这一点都成立。因此，事实上的不能——例如，被教唆方没有能力或意图实施该罪行——不是一种抗辩理由。

在本案中，当艺术家请求朋友帮助她实施盗窃罪的那一刻，教唆罪就已经构成。因此，即使朋友没有能力或意图打开仓库或不锁仓库，该艺术家也构成了教唆罪。

(选项A) 犯罪未遂发生在被告(1)具有实施犯罪的特定意图，(2)为促进犯罪实施了公开行为，但(3)未能完成犯罪时。根据普通法的“危险接近”测试，公开行为必须使被告足够接近完成犯罪。但在本案中，该艺术家在采取任何使其接近盗窃画作的行动之前就被逮捕了。

(选项B) 普通法上的贿赂罪是指为影响公职人员履行其公共或法律职责而进行的腐败性价值支付。保安不属于公职人员，因此该艺术家没有犯贿赂罪。

(选项C) 普通法对共谋罪的双边理论要求证明至少有两个犯罪意图。因此，如果另一位共谋者假装同意（如本案所示），被告则不能被定罪。

教学目标：当一个人(1)引诱、鼓励、请求或命令他人犯罪，(2)并具有希望被教唆的罪行得以实施的特定意图时，教唆罪即告成立。事实上的不能并非教唆罪的抗辩理由。

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Inchoate Crimes (未遂/不完整犯罪)
正确答案：D (Solicitation)

本题考查的是教唆罪 (Solicitation) 的构成要件以及普通法下共谋罪的特殊规则。

为什么是教唆罪 (Solicitation)?
根据普通法 (Common Law)，教唆罪的成立只需要满足两个条件：
  1. 行为 (Actus Reus): 引诱、鼓励、请求或命令他人犯罪。
  2. 意图 (Mens Rea): 具有希望该犯罪被实际实施的特定意图 (Specific Intent)。
关键点：教唆罪是一种“言语即行为”的犯罪。一旦艺术家开口请求朋友帮忙并意图实施盗窃，犯罪即告完成 (Completed)。
事实不能 (Factual Impossibility) 不是抗辩理由： 哪怕朋友根本没有钥匙，或者朋友根本不想帮忙，都不影响艺术家构成教唆罪。
为什么不是共谋罪 (Conspiracy)?
陷阱分析： 很多考生看到“两人对话”和“同意”会误选 C。
题目明确指出适用普通法 (Common Law)。
  • 双边理论 (Bilateral Approach): 普通法要求共谋必须有至少两个“有罪的头脑” (Two Guilty Minds)。
  • 假装同意 (Feigned Agreement): 本案中，朋友是保安，他只是假装同意，实际上想报警。因此，只有艺术家一个人有犯罪意图。
  • 结论： 1个真意图 + 1个假意图 ≠ 普通法下的共谋。
*注：如果是《模范刑法典》(MPC)，采用单边理论 (Unilateral Approach)，则可能构成共谋，但MBE题目默认普通法规则，除非另有说明。
其他选项排除
A. 盗窃未遂 (Attempted Larceny)
错误原因：未遂需要“公开行为” (Overt Act) 且该行为必须“危险地接近” (Dangerous Proximity) 犯罪完成。仅仅是“寻找帮手”通常被视为预备行为 (Preparation)，尚未达到未遂的标准。且她在实施进一步行动前已被捕。
B. 贿赂 (Bribery)
错误原因：普通法下的贿赂罪严格限于涉及公职人员 (Public Official)。博物馆保安是私人雇员，不符合主体资格。
💡 MBE 破题金手指

遇到“一人提议，另一人假装同意并报警”的剧情：

  1. 如果是Common Law → 选 Solicitation (教唆)，不选 Conspiracy。
  2. 如果是MPC (或题目未强调Common Law且选项无Solicitation) → 可能选 Conspiracy (单边理论)。
  3. Merger Doctrine (合并原则)： 如果犯罪真的完成了，Solicitation 会合并入主罪；但本题中盗窃未发生，所以只定教唆。

The police had been tracking a businessman who used his fast-food chain as a front for selling cocaine. The cocaine was produced by a chemist in a lab hidden inside the factory where the fast food was made. The cocaine was then shipped along with the food to a fast-food restaurant, where the manager of the restaurant would divide the cocaine up into smaller quantities for sale to individual customers. Due to the large-scale operations, the businessman, the chemist, and the manager did not know one another. One day, an undercover police officer came to the restaurant and purchased cocaine from the manager. Upon completion of the transaction, the manager was arrested for conspiracy to sell cocaine.
Is the manager likely guilty of conspiracy to sell cocaine?

choices.a: No, because the manager, the businessman, and the chemist did not know one another.
choices.b: No, because there was no agreement between the manager, the businessman, and the chemist to sell cocaine.
choices.c: Yes, because the manager, the businessman, and the chemist had the general intent to sell cocaine.
choices.d: Yes, because there was a community of interest between the manager, the businessman, and the chemist to sell cocaine.

警方一直在追踪一名商人，该商人利用其快餐连锁店作为贩卖可卡因的掩护。可卡因由一名化学家在一家生产快餐食品的工厂内的秘密实验室内生产。然后，可卡因随同食品被运送至一家快餐店，该店的经理会将可卡因分成小份，出售给个人顾客。由于该行动规模庞大，商人、化学家和经理彼此互不相识。一天，一名卧底警察来到该餐厅，并从经理处购买了可卡因。交易完成后，该经理因涉嫌共谋贩卖可卡因而被逮捕。

该经理是否可能构成共谋贩卖可卡因罪？
options:
A. No, because the manager, the businessman, and the chemist did not know one another.
不会，因为经理、商人和化学家彼此互不相识。

B. No, because there was no agreement between the manager, the businessman, and the chemist to sell cocaine.
不会，因为经理、商人和化学家之间没有贩卖可卡因的协议。

C. Yes, because the manager, the businessman, and the chemist had the general intent to sell cocaine.
会，因为经理、商人和化学家具有贩卖可卡因的概括意图。

D. Yes, because there was a community of interest between the manager, the businessman, and the chemist to sell cocaine.
会，因为经理、商人和化学家之间在贩卖可卡因方面存在利益共同体。
data.explanation:
Conspiracy , at its core, is an agreement between two or more persons to commit a crime. A conspiracy can exist among individuals who do not know each other if there is a community of interest in achieving the objective of the conspiracy. A community of interest is usually established through a chain relationship where each alleged conspirator played a role or served as a link in the chain in reaching the conspiracy's objective.

Here, the businessman, the chemist, and the manager did not know each other. However, they each played a role in reaching the objective of the conspiracy - selling cocaine. The businessman owned the fast-food chain used as a front for selling cocaine, the chemist produced the cocaine, and the manager divided it for individual sale. Due to this community of interest, the manager is likely guilty of conspiracy (Choice A).

(Choice B) For a conspiracy, an agreement need not be specifically articulated (eg, verbally or in writing). It can be inferred from the concerted actions of the alleged conspirators (as seen here).

(Choice C) Conspiracy requires the specific intent (not general intent) to agree to and to achieve the criminal objective.

Educational objective: A conspiracy can exist among individuals who do not know each other when there is a community of interest in the achievement of the objective of the conspiracy. A community of interest typically exists when each alleged conspirator plays a role in reaching that objective.

共谋罪 (Conspiracy) 的核心是两人或两人以上为实施犯罪而达成的协议 (agreement)。即使个人之间互不相识，只要为实现共谋目标存在利益共同体 (community of interest)，共谋 (conspiracy) 仍然可以成立。利益共同体通常通过一种链条关系 (chain relationship) 建立，其中每位被指控的共谋者在达成共谋目标的过程中都扮演了一个角色或充当了链条中的一个环节。

在本案中，商人、化学家和经理彼此互不相识。然而，他们每个人都在达成共谋目标——贩卖可卡因——的过程中扮演了角色。商人拥有用作贩卖可卡因掩护的快餐连锁店，化学家生产可卡因，而经理则将其分装以供个人销售。由于存在此利益共同体，该经理可能构成共谋罪，因此(选项A)的理由不成立。

(选项B) 对于共谋罪，协议 (agreement) 无需明确表达（例如，口头或书面）。它可以从被指控的共谋者的一致行动中推断出来（如本案所示）。

(选项C) 共谋罪 (Conspiracy) 要求具有达成协议和实现犯罪目标的特定意图 (specific intent)（而非概括意图 general intent）。

教学目的：当为实现共谋目标而存在利益共同体 (community of interest) 时，即使个人之间互不相识，共谋罪 (conspiracy) 依然可以成立。当每位被指控的共谋者在达成该目标的过程中都扮演一个角色时，通常就存在利益共同体。

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Inchoate Crimes: Conspiracy (共谋罪)
核心考点：链式共谋 (Chain Conspiracy)

本题考查的是共谋罪中经典的“链式关系” (Chain Relationship)。即使共谋者之间互不相识，只要他们为了一个共同的非法目标而形成利益共同体 (Community of Interest)，共谋罪即可成立。

非法毒品分销链条
化学家 (Chemist)
制造毒品
商人 (Businessman)
提供掩护与运输
经理 (Manager)
分销给顾客 (本案被告)
🔗
虽然互不相识，但每一环的成功都依赖于整个链条的运作。

为什么选 D？

正确答案是 D。这基于著名的判例原则（如 United States v. Bruno）。

在毒品走私或分销案件中，通常被视为链式共谋 (Chain Conspiracy)。虽然经理可能不知道化学家或商人的具体身份，但他知道：

  1. 毒品不会凭空出现（必然有人生产和运输）；
  2. 他是这个庞大非法计划中的一环；
  3. 他的成功（销售获利）依赖于其他人的成功。

这种相互依赖关系构成了利益共同体 (Community of Interest)。法律推定这种情况下存在“协议”，因为每个参与者都通过行动加入到了这个持续的非法计划中。

干扰项陷阱

选项 A 错误 互不相识 (Did not know one another)：
这是 MBE 最常见的干扰项。共谋不需要所有成员面对面开会。在链式共谋中，只要知道自己是更大计划的一部分即可，无需知道其他同伙的具体身份。
选项 B 错误 没有协议 (No agreement)：
共谋罪的“协议”可以是推定的 (Implied)。通过各方协调一致的行动（Concerted actions）——生产、运输、分销——可以推断出协议的存在。
选项 C 错误 概括意图 (General Intent)：
这是一个法律术语陷阱。共谋罪是特定意图犯罪 (Specific Intent Crime)。被告必须具有达成协议的意图 以及 实现非法目标的意图。选项 C 错误地将其描述为概括意图。
💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip):
遇到涉及多人分工的犯罪（特别是毒品、走私），首先判断结构：
  • 链式 (Chain): 像本题，彼此依赖，通常视为一个大共谋。
  • 轮辐式 (Wheel): 一个中心人物与多个独立互不相干的人交易（如高利贷者借钱给互不认识的借款人）。如果没有共同利益，通常视为多个独立的小共谋。

questions.question:
An 18-year-old female and a 15-year-old male, who had known each other since early childhood, agreed to have sexual intercourse and did so. The applicable jurisdiction defines rape as "sexual intercourse with another person (i) without that person's consent or (ii) who is less than 16 years old." This jurisdiction also follows the common-law approach to conspiracy.
Can the female properly be charged with conspiracy to commit rape?

choices.a: No, because the male is a member of the protected class.
choices.b: No, because the sexual intercourse was consensual.
choices.c: Yes, because the female knew that the male was only 15 years old.
choices.d: Yes, because the male was less than 16 years old.
